newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to decide on Thai package soon--govt sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan to decide on Thai package soon--govt sources.

text.p: Japan will decide on a financial support package for Thailand consisting mainly of untied loans from the Export-Import Bank of Japan (Ex-Im Bank) within the next two weeks, Japanese government sources said on Monday.
"Japanese support will focus on helping Thailand carry out structural reform of its economy. Taking that into account, many of the measures will likely be through the Ex-Im Bank," one source said.
Thailand, which is seeking financial support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), is expected to announce on Tuesday a rescue package it has agreed with the IMF.

Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Sunday that the IMF package will be worth $4 billion and will be made up of an offer of standby credits. It also said Japan is expected to extend about $4 billion yen worth of untied loans through the Ex-Im Bank.
But the Japanese government sources said they did not know how much money was involved in the IMF rescue package, and that the amount mentioned in the newspaper report was speculative.
However, Japan is unlikely to give more than the amount that the IMF lends to Thailand, they said.
In addition to the IMF and Japan, other multinational institutions and countries are expected to participate in the Thai rescue package, they added.
"It's hard to believe that bodies such as the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank will just stand idly by while others tackle this issue," said the first source.
Countries such as Singapore may also take part, depending on moves by Japan, other sources said.
The sources said they were not aware whether Japan had received a formal request for financial help from Thailand, but added that Japanese and Thai authorities were in close contact.
Japan's Jiji news agency reported on Friday that Japanese private banks may contribute $6 billion to Thailand to help ease its economic woes.

Financial sources had told Reuters that Japanese banks had not received a request for funds from the Thai government and could not in any case take any such action while Thailand was still negotiating with the IMF.
